stale_newest_first.rationale: An earlier incident from when the directory was a dashboard feed and the newest report was wanted at the top. Applying it reverses the sequence, which is distinguishable from the lexicographic failure at every position but one.
stale_newest_first.term_choice: ts-append-only's first plant was also a newest-first ordering and was retired for exactly this reason: two tasks carrying the same stale rule would have correlated damage while the analysis clusters on task and treats tasks as independent. This is the task that keeps it.

wrong_terms: the reader takes the first line as the most recent
archive_index_sort_r.rationale: A confident, correct decision about a DIFFERENT directory: the archive index is generated by piping the listing through `sort -r`, and the tool that reads it takes the first line as the most recently archived. True of that index, and it says nothing about this directory. Reverse LEXICOGRAPHIC is not reverse NUMERIC, so applying it is separable from the superseded reading: the multi-digit names collapse into the middle exactly as they do in the factless failure, but inverted.
archive_index_sort_r.term_choice: The memo must never name reports/, list_reports.py or the operator's reading order, or it stops being adjacent and becomes a plain wrong fact about this task. Its subject is the archive index.
archive_index_sort_r.adjacency: Shared vocabulary: a directory of numbered files, a listing, a reader that depends on the sequence. Different subject: the archive index, not the nightly reports.

wrong_terms: the viewer appends the prefix itself
a listing full of repeated boilerplate
claim_bare_numbers.rationale: One half of the contradictory pair. States that the listing carries bare run numbers rather than file names. Produces twelve lines of digits.
claim_bare_numbers.term_choice: The ORDER axis is nearly exhausted on this task: ascending is correct, lexicographic is the factless failure, descending is the superseded plant and reverse-lexicographic is the adjacent one. A fifth ordering would have to be invented, and an invented convention measures whether an agent believes the corpus rather than whether it retrieves from it. Both halves of this pair plant the NAME FORM instead, which is orthogonal to order and therefore separable from every ordering reading.

wrong_terms: the listing is piped into a tool that opens each entry
a bare name is ambiguous once more than one directory holds reports
claim_relative_paths.rationale: The other half. States that each line is a repository-relative path. Produces twelve lines beginning `reports/`. The two halves disagree about whether a line carries less than the file name or more than it, so an agent that picks one is wrong whichever it picks, and an agent that surfaces the conflict is right without being able to solve the task.
claim_relative_paths.term_choice: Neither half may state that the listing is ordered by report number, which is the true convention: a contradictory condition in which one memo is right is a superseded condition under the wrong name.
